subject: function:init_next_level
value:
PHASE-0 VERDICT of work_claim.split-map-correction.20260904.v1, which made this the gate on everything else. THE ONE CONTRADICTION named by claim.BE_the-enemy-gauntworld-blob-aliasing-is-not-aliasing-it-is-a-text-split-misassignment-inside-gamemain.20260904.v1 -- 'init_next_level 0x8005638C is PDB-GAMEMAIN.OBJ but sits between two gauntworld.obj functions in .text AND reads base 0x80112788 (gauntworld's section) at its 17 converted literal sites' -- RESOLVES AS READING (i): the function at 0x8005638C belongs to gauntworld.obj, the GC symbol name `init_next_level` is a name-only mis-adoption of GAMEMAIN.OBJ's static of the same name, and the base-per-section law is NOT falsified. The blueprint scored this 2:1; measured at HEAD 1a7f0393e it is 5:0, and four of the five axes are retail bytes rather than a PDB row.

AXIS 1 -- .text CONTIGUITY. 0x8005638C sits strictly between FindWobjWanim 0x80055CB8 and NextWorldLevel 0x80057E6C, every named function in that run mapping to gauntworld.obj. An object's .text is one contiguous run, so for this function to be GAMEMAIN.OBJ's, GAMEMAIN.OBJ's .text would have to be discontiguous. It cannot be.

AXIS 2 -- extabindex CONTIGUITY, a SECOND section and an axis the blueprint did not name. `build/GUNE5D/asm/game/game/gamemain.s` (the dtk split at the OLD boundaries) shows this function's exception index entry as `@eti_80009D30` -- `.4byte init_next_level_8005638C / .4byte 0x0000030C / .4byte "@etb_80006340"` -- sitting between fn_80055F68's `@eti_80009D24` and fn_80056698's `@eti_80009D3C`, inside the unbroken run 0x80009D00 (DoWorldAnimation) .. 0x80009D9C (fn_80057F44 + 0xC). The same contiguity argument applies to extabindex as to .text, independently.

AXIS 3 -- extab CONTIGUITY. Its table `@etb_80006340` lies inside 0x80006320..0x80006388, the run whose first entry (0x80006320) belongs to DoWorldAnimation and whose last (0x80006380+8) belongs to fn_80057F44.

AXIS 4 -- .rodata PARTITION, measured per function over the whole region with a census of every lbl_8011xxxx a function references in the dtk split asm (enemy.s / gamemain.s / gauntworld.s). The three blocks partition EXACTLY and the boundary is sharp: the HIGHEST datum any real-GAMEMAIN.OBJ function reads is 0x8011277C (init_thermometer, "THERMCOL", 9 bytes, then a 3-byte pad `gap_06_80112785_rodata` to 0x80112788); the LOWEST datum any gauntworld-block function reads is 0x80112788 ("levels/level%s"). init_next_level reads 0x80112788 and nothing below it, and it shares that single 0x24C-byte dtk run with world_update, fn_80057024, PrintWorldMemSizes, ResolveWorldData and ResolveWorldDataPointers -- i.e. with gauntworld.c's own already-assigned functions.

AXIS 5 -- .sdata2 POOL INTERLEAVE, also new. The same census over 0x80346700..0x80346D00 gives gamemain-block entries 0x80346AB0..0x80346BD8 and gauntworld-block entries 0x80346BE0..0x80346CB4, disjoint at 0x80346BE0; init_next_level's two entries are 0x80346C00 and 0x80346C04, and gauntworld.c's own ResolveWorldDataPointers reads 0x80346BE0 and 0x80346C70 -- inside the block's range. Two objects' .sdata2 runs cannot interleave, so the block and gauntworld.c are one object.

AXIS 5b -- LINKAGE, the axis that also refutes the PDB row on its own terms. Xbox GAMEMAIN.OBJ's init_next_level is `L` (static). The GC function at 0x8005638C is CALLED from 0x80053C2C, inside LoadTowerAndSelect, which is in the real GAMEMAIN.OBJ block -- a call that crosses the object boundary and therefore cannot target a static. The GC symbols.txt entry says `scope:local`, which is wrong for the same reason.

AGAINST, in full: one `method: exact_name` PDB link at `confidence: 0.5` whose own note reads 'Exact spelling only; target behavior and platform applicability remain unverified', to a symbol that is static on both sides -- i.e. a name with no linkage evidence at all.

NAMING HYPOTHESIS, NOT ADOPTED. Reversing the GC block and aligning it against gauntworld.obj's PDB roster gives an exact seven-row run -- FindWobjWanim/FindWobjWanim, DoWorldAnimation/DoWorldAnimation, WorldObjectExplode/WorldObjectExplode, WorldExplosion/WorldExplosion, fn_80055F68(0x404)/LoadGauntWorldDone(0x38F), fn_8005636C(0x20)/BGLoadFile(0x16), init_next_level(0x30C)/LoadGauntWorldStart(0x2DC) -- which puts this function at LoadGauntWorldStart's index with a plausible size, and its body (a boss-wad switch calling CritterLoadFile("critter","dragon.wad") per claim.FS_gamemain-boss-wad-switch-case-values-are-e_e_tpye-enumerators.20260904.v1) fits that name. NOT ADOPTED: position is evidence, not proof, and the rename needs a caller-context pass of its own. The symbol keeps its current spelling.
